lessons.title: Applying Your Confidence

memory_verse.text: Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.

getting_started: The topic of faith can stir quite a debate among Christians. While some define faith as absolute assurance in a particular outcome, others see it strictly as a reverent submission to the inevitable. This study attempts to balance these views, focusing on faith as it is described and defined in Hebrews 11. While it does explore supernatural forms of confidence, this "faith chapter" also examines what Christians are to do when things don't work out as expected.

option.label: Activity Option
option.note: Genuine faith should have visible effects on our lives.

overview: What the Book of Hebrews says about faith.
How you can have more faith in your life.
How you can use faith to help others.

discussion.heading: God is worthy of our faith.

questions.text: Read Heb 11:1-3,6. Describe some ways people exercise faith.
questions.leader_note: Note: People often believe others love them. Though people can't "see" love, they have faith that it exists because of how those people have treated them.

questions.text: What determines the quality of someone's faith? That is, what makes the faith turn out good or bad?
questions.leader_note: Note: A person's faith is only as good as the person or the object in which it's placed.

questions.text: Read Heb 11:4-5, 7-8, 29-30. Using the accompanying questions as a guide, what can you learn from the examples of each of the following people in a way that demonstrate faith in God:

bullets.title: Abel
bullets.text: What are some sincere ways a teen could honour God that would require faith? What could a teen offer God that would cause Him to speak well of him or her as He did of Abel?

bullets.title: Enoch
bullets.text: In what ways do you think Enoch pleased God so much that God took him without his seeing death? How could we strive to please God in that way?

bullets.title: Noah
bullets.text: Considering Noah's example, how does your faith affect those around you?

bullets.title: Abraham
bullets.text: How do you know what actions to take when trusting God?

questions.text: What do you think most people mean when they say that faith is, or should be, a personal thing?
questions.leader_note: Hint: People often use this as an argument or excuse that people should keep their faith to themselves and not try to impose their beliefs on others.

discussion.heading: Faith brings power.

questions.text: Read Heb 11:32-35. Why might some of the miracles mentioned in this passage seem to require more faith or be more miraculous than the others?
Read Heb 11:35-40. What normally happens when people trust God and He doesn't do what they expect?
questions.leader_note: Note: We must not allow our circumstances to dictate our levels of faith; for God calls us to trust Him – not in a particular outcome.

questions.text: What should you do when you have faith in God and He allows something terrible to occur?

discussion.note: Having true faith does not mean knowing what's going to happen. Instead, it means trusting a situation to God and acting confidently on what He has told you – regardless of your situation. Therefore, one of the first step toward gaining more faith is taking the time and effort to listen to Him.

lessons.act: Read Romans 10:17. If faith comes by hearing, then what and whom we listen to does matter. If we want to increase our faith, we must honestly evaluate the sources of information and opinions we allow into our lives, no matter how harmless some of them might seem. So, we must determine by the Word of God to take control of our own outlook and refuse to let the world or circumstance decide how we should think and act.

lessons.title: Change Your Perspective

memory_verse.text: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

getting_started: Not everything is exactly as it seems on the surface – especially in spiritual matters. Some things that may seem harmless can be destructive, while things that seem disastrous can make a positive turnaround when left in God's hands. Sometimes, it's simply a matter of perspective. As you go into this study, pray that God will help you see your life from His eternal perspective.
overview: How God is faithful to finish what HE starts in your life.
How our attitudes through difficult time can attract unbelievers to Christ.
How God will fulfil His plans in spite of the motives and intentions of people.
The responsibility and privilege of Christians to stand for, as well as suffer for, their faith and identification with Christ.

discussion.heading: People in Process
discussion.intro: Read Php 1:3-6. Note that while appreciating the Philippian church for their support to his ministry, Paul was confident not only in what God has done for the people in saving them, but also what He will continue to do for them as they remain faithful to God and His work.

questions.text: Why do people sometimes start things that they don't finish?
If God has the ability to finish everything, why are people "incomplete" in so many ways? Why does He take people through a process?
questions.leader_note: Note: People develop stronger character, faith, and understanding through various life experiences.

questions.text: How should God's promise and ability to finish affect our attitude toward ourselves and others?
questions.leader_note: Hint: It should make us more patient and keep us from passing premature judgment on people's ability, character, or motives. God's promise should also make us more hopeful.

questions.text: Read Php 1:12-14. Often, when people suffer or are persecuted for a cause, others are emboldened to take up the cause as well. Why is this, when it might seem more logical that fear would drive people away or cause them to keep quiet?
Describe forms of persecution that you or other Christians might experience and how God's kingdom can advance as a result.
Read Php 1:15-19. Why is it so easy to be envious of another Christian's successes or opportunities? How is that attitude destructive and immature?
How can we maintain good attitude toward those who seem to be more "blessed"? How can we become better at promoting the gifts and ministries of others?
questions.leader_note: Note: God doesn't respect one person's faith or productivity more than another's, as long as each is being and doing what God intended.

questions.text: Read Php 1:19-26. Why does the prospect of death frighten most people? Why should it be different for a Christian?
How should the inevitability of death affect our lives currently?
questions.leader_note: Hint: We should live life to the fullest, not worrying about things that will eventually be meaningless. We should be more deliberate in influencing others toward Christ since they could die without Christ at any time.

discussion.heading: Purposeful Pain

questions.text: Read Php 1:27-30. Describe some of the positive results of Christians suffering for their faith.

discussion.note: Suffering for our faith doesn't mean we have done something wrong. The opposite is often true – it may verify that we have been faithful.

lessons.act: Spend a few moments in prayer, asking God to work things out in your life for His own glory and help you keep a good attitude in the meantime.
